definition: An AI system that works towards a goal in several steps, choosing tools to call (such as search, a calculator or code) and deciding what to do next from the results.
The mechanism that lets each token in a transformer weigh every other token when building its own representation, so context such as which noun a pronoun refers to is captured.
The method for training neural networks that passes the error backwards from the output and calculates how much each weight contributed to it, so every weight can be adjusted.
A short piece of a longer document. RAG systems split documents into chunks so that only the relevant pieces are retrieved and sent to the model.
The maximum number of tokens a language model can take into account at once, including both the prompt and the answer it writes.
A score between two vectors that measures whether they point in the same direction. Near 1 means very similar meaning; near 0 means unrelated.
A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a piece of text, an image or another item. Items with similar meanings get similar lists.
Getting a model to do a new task by showing it a few worked examples inside the prompt, without changing any of its parameters.
Training an already trained model further on a smaller, focused dataset to change its behaviour, style or skill at a particular task.
Graphics processing unit. A chip that performs many simple calculations in parallel, which makes it well suited to training and running neural networks.
A fluent and confident answer from an AI model that is false or not supported by any source.
A neural network, usually a transformer with billions of parameters, trained on very large amounts of text to predict the next token.
One of the numbers inside a neural network that is learned during training. Large language models have billions of them.
The text given to a language model as input. In RAG, the prompt contains the instruction, the retrieved chunks and the question.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Finding the passages most relevant to a question and placing them in the prompt so the model answers from them instead of from memory.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback. People compare model answers, a reward model learns their preferences, and the language model is trained to produce answers the reward model rates highly.
A setting that controls how random a model's word choices are. Low temperature gives predictable text; high temperature gives more varied text.
The unit of text a language model reads and writes: a word, part of a word or a punctuation mark. In English a token is about four characters on average.
The neural network architecture, introduced in 2017, that is built around attention and is the basis of almost all modern language models.
A store for embeddings that can quickly find the stored vectors closest to a new vector, used by RAG systems to retrieve relevant chunks.
Asking a model to do a task with only an instruction and no worked examples in the prompt.
